items.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2
items.summary: Anthropic announced two new models with gains in coding, reasoning and vision. Fable 5.2 is live in the Claude Platform and Claude Code, up to 30% faster than Fable 5.1 and priced at $8/$40 per 1M tokens, down from $10/$50.

reception.summary: Repliers mostly cheered the launch and the price cut, asked when Mythos reaches regular users and whether usage limits reset; nobody reported benchmark problems yet.

items.title: Meta ships Muse Ember, a small 1M-context agent model at $0.10/$0.50 per 1M tokens
items.summary: Meta released its smallest model, aimed at tool-calling agent work, test runs and targeted code fixes, with 1M-token context and native text, image, audio and video input. Arena and Vals place it ahead of other small models on cost per task; it is API-only so far.

doubt.pushback: Repliers and quote posts note it only ties Claude Haiku 5.5 on the Artificial Analysis index and loses to Haiku on FrontierCode; the strongest numbers are Meta's own or cost-per-task, and weights are not available for local use.

reception.summary: Mostly positive on price and cost per task, with questions about tool-failure recovery, long-context pricing and local availability; no one reported a hands-on run in the replies read.

items.title: AirCaps A5S Async v1 takes first place on Voice Arena diarization plus ASR board
items.summary: On 139 held-out multi-speaker conversations, the speech-to-text model that labels who said each word scored 23.89% cpWER, ahead of 14 other systems, with a 95% interval of 19.47% to 28.58%. A commentator says the team published code, dataset recipes and raw API responses.

items.title: Private OCR eval of 9 open-weight models on 338 scanned 20th-century pages
items.summary: Pairwise VLM-judge comparison across 10,730 judgments found small models on top: LightOn OCR-3-0.8B and Falcon-OCR 270M. Tiling added about 130 rating points to one model; the author notes the judge is not yet validated on pages like these.

doubt.pushback: Author's own caveat: judge validated on 19th-century books, not these pages.

items.title: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash reaches 438 tok/s on 4 DGX Sparks with 16 users in a community repo
items.summary: A repo for serving the model on four DGX Sparks reports 438 tok/s for 16 identical prompts and 380 tok/s with different prompts, over 2x upstream; the poster notes the single-user speed barely changed.

doubt.pushback: Poster flags that the headline figure uses 16 copies of the same prompt.

items.title: PostTrainBench v1.2 adds Gemini 4 Argon (40.4%) and Muse Wonder (24.2%)
items.summary: New benchmark results for how well agents post-train models: Gemini 4 Argon scores 40.4% and Muse Wonder 24.2%.

items.title: World Labs Atlas ranks first in Rapidata camera-movement benchmark across 19 models
items.summary: A third-party human-preference benchmark (600 prompts, 513K+ judgments) rated Atlas best at following camera instructions among 19 world and video models.

doubt.pushback: Result reported by the model's own maker; method is in a linked thread not read.

items.title: Hume Audio Decision API launches with a no-account demo
items.summary: Hume released an API that answers questions about audio, such as detecting sarcasm, and offers 250,000 free tokens (about 50 minutes of audio) without an account.

items.title: Hermes Cloud agents open in a browser tab with the Hermes Desktop interface
items.summary: Nous now hosts personal agents that launch from Nous Portal by choosing a name and a model, and run in the browser with the same UI as the desktop app.

items.title: Nvidia builds a Gemma 4 E4B robot assistant that runs on an 8GB Jetson
items.summary: Per the Gemma team, Nvidia fit live conversation, tool calls, animations and a vision model on one 8GB Jetson using Gemma 4 E4B; shown as a demo clip only.

doubt.pushback: Demo clip only in the posts read; no repo or numbers seen.
